name: Mesalamine
summary: Topically active 5-aminosalicylate acting from the gut lumen — first-line induction and maintenance therapy for mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis.
mechanism: Acts luminally on the colonic mucosa to suppress local inflammation (inhibition of prostaglandin/leukotriene synthesis, PPAR-γ activation); minimal systemic anti-inflammatory effect.

pharmacokinetics.bioavailability: Oral: ~20–30% systemically absorbed; acts topically in the colon
pharmacokinetics.duration: Formulation-dependent (once to three times daily dosing)
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Acetylation in gut mucosa and liver

dosing.adult: Ulcerative colitis: 1.2–4.8 g daily in divided doses, depending on formulation and severity; rectal forms (enema/suppository) for distal disease
dosing.renalAdjustment: Use with caution; monitor renal function

safety.pregnancy: Commonly continued through pregnancy in IBD; no major teratogenicity demonstrated
safety.lactation: Small amounts in breast milk; generally considered compatible (rare infant diarrhea)
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to salicylates or mesalamine products
warnings: Interstitial nephritis — check renal function at baseline and periodically
Do not switch formulations casually — release sites differ
safety.overdose: Salicylate-like effects (tinnitus, nephrotoxicity) at very high doses — supportive care

clinicalPearls: Different formulations release at different sites (pH-dependent, time-dependent, MMX) — switching brands without thought can change efficacy
It works from the luminal side — rectal forms beat oral for distal disease
good: First-line UC therapy with minimal systemic toxicity
bad: Renal impairment (monitor); salicylate allergy; severe flares needing systemic therapy
